name: backlog
description: A week's backlog for a three-person team: 15 bugs, 5 requirements, 2 architecture changes. Agents do the work; the house rules (a data file) decide what needs a person; the desk is where people decide the rest. Bugs: clean fixes land on their own, lock-ins and slop go to the lead. Requirements: both ICs accept the agent's criteria. Architecture: both ICs advise, the lead decides, and the decision is written down.

neurons.description: Bug reports, one trace each. A P4 is injected with a smaller budget.
New requirements from product, one trace each.
Architecture change requests, one trace each.
The bug-fixing agent: answers a patch (canned and invented in this demo).
The house rules as data: a dependency nobody chose is a lock-in; a second config or a duplicate helper is slop.
Quiet for a clean patch; for a flagged one, the lead's ask with the findings.
The lead decides a flagged fix: land it anyway, or send it back.
Lands a fix: clean ones on their own, flagged ones only on the lead's word. An effect.
The spec agent: acceptance criteria for a requirement, put to both ICs.
Both ICs have answered: scheduled when both accepted, else back to product.
The architecture agent: drafts the decision record for both ICs.
Both ICs have advised: the lead's ask, with their advice.
The lead adopts or rejects the change.
Writes the decision record, adopted or rejected. An effect.
